title: Economy Slice Design Lab Notes
summary: Working notes from a 2-day design lab focused on a compact console view that surfaces per-invocation "economy slices" — the minimal token-level explanations and latency breakdowns engineers need during debugging and SLO investigations.
audience: console product team, design, applied-ml, solutions engineering
primary_goals: Surface per-invocation token cost attribution in a compact, scannable view
Provide a latency waterfall tied to token spans and model execution phases
Enable fast triage: identify expensive prompts, hot prefixes, or model variants
Keep UI lightweight for high-cardinality traces (avoid full token stream render by default)
design_assumptions: Most users want a 1–3 item summary first, then expandable detail
Token-level detail is rarely needed for every invocation — provide progressive disclosure
We have reliable per-request telemetry: token counts, kernel time, KV cache hits, batching metadata
Customers care about both cost delta and latency delta when comparing rollouts
wireframe_highlights: Compact card header: invocation id, model variant, start time, overall cost, overall latency
Economy-meter: a compact sparkline showing cost per 100 tokens in the last minute for the route
Token-slice summary row: show top 3 'hot slices' (prefix, generation, post-process) with % cost and ms
Expandable token-lane: toggles between 'summary', 'span waterfall', and 'full token inspector', default = summary
Span waterfall bands color-coded: tokenization, prefix-embedding lookup, attention, KV-apply, decode kernel
Action buttons: pin-as-alert, open-eval, create-rollback, attach-to-incident
annotated-wire-notes: Left column: filters & quick compares (time range, model variant, route, customer tier)
Mid pane: invocation list with inline economy badges (red/yellow/green), tap to expand into detail card
Detail card: three tab states — 'Econ summary', 'Latency waterfall', 'Token autopsy'
Token autopsy: virtualized list with inline cost attribution and ability to search for substrings (prefix matches)
Keyboard shortcuts: quick-toggle detail (space), pin (p), compare (c)
Small-screen behavior: collapse filters into a drawer, prioritize the invocation list and summary card
backlog_candidates: ECO-1: Economy-meter lightweight prototype (sparkline + percentile overlay)
ECO-2: Backend API spec for per-token attribution (agree on schema: token_span_id, cost_usd, kernel_ms, cache_hit)
ECO-3: Waterfall visual component with phase grouping and mini-histograms
ECO-4: Token autopsy virtualization + server-side pagination
ECO-5: Compare mode: side-by-side two invocations and delta highlighting
ECO-6: Alerting hook: create cost-regression alert from invocation card
ECO-7: UX accessibility pass: color-blind-friendly palette and high contrast mode
risks_and_constraints: High-cardinality token dumps could overwhelm browser memory — need virtualization and server-side summarization
Per-token cost attribution requires additional telemetry; sampling may be necessary for tiered plans
Latency attributions depend on accurate kernel tagging which requires small runtime changes from serving-runtime team
Privacy: some customers don't want raw token text in console — need redaction toggle and opt-out
open_questions: Q1: Should per-token text be stored by default or only on-demand? (security + storage tradeoff)
Q2: How do we represent batched requests that share KV cache: attribution per sub-request vs shared cost?
Q3: Target SLAs — acceptable latency for unfolding the detail card on large invocations?
Q4: Rollout strategy — feature-gate to Dedicated/Private customers first?
decisions_made: Decision 1: default view will be summary + span waterfall; full token inspector is opt-in
Decision 2: add 'cost delta' indicator when a model variant mismatch is detected on the route
Decision 3: wire a backend sampling flag; store full token traces for 72 hours for hosted, configurable for Dedicated
next_steps: Proto: design to produce a high-fidelity Figma flow for the detail card (owner: Lena) — due 2026-01-29
Infra: SRE + serving-runtime to review kernel tagging changes and provide a timeline (owner: Owen) — request by 2026-02-05
API: draft telemetry schema for per-token attribution and publish Confluence spec (owner: Marcus) — draft by 2026-02-12
Research: run 2-week sampling experiment on production traces to estimate storage and cost (owner: Priya) — kick off by 2026-02-01
Backlog: triage ECO items and convert top 3 into JIRA issues for sprint planning
notes_to_self: Keep language simple in the header — engineers want immediate signal: $ / ms / verdict
Avoid full token streams by default — show aggregated spans and let users drill in
Collect feedback from Solutions Eng on the compare mode — they often need 3+ invocations in a single view
Double-check privacy policy impact before enabling default token storage
